source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.short_quote: While they are matutine and preceding the Sun, they are masculine; when vespertine and following the Sun, they become feminine.

normalized_rule: Classify a planet as masculine when it is matutine and precedes the Sun, and as feminine when it is vespertine and follows the Sun.
synthesis_notes: This is a source-specific solar-relation classification, not a later generic orientality rule.
review_notes: Keep separate from the horizon-quadrant oriental/occidental classification in the same chapter; the two source statements are not interchangeable.
transmission_notes: This is the Sun-relative masculine/feminine passage in the Ashmand/Proclus transmission. It is distinct from the following horizon-quadrant statement; certainty is not certainty about an autograph of Ptolemy.
